A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research framework, renamed LH-Deception in v3. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulations across 11 models, Startup Consulting and Activity Planning results, pressure/category controls, and qualitative trajectory analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds human validation, a single-turn versus full-context auditor comparison, and a no-event condition.

M1.justification: The task/event system, performer-supervisor loop, memory, state updates, and full-history auditing remain unchanged. The supervisor and auditor prompts in Appendices A.4–A.5 match. Single-turn auditing is introduced as an experimental control.

E1.justification: The two domains and their 14-task streams are retained. Figure 5 adds a 'None' condition without external events, extending environmental coverage. DeceptionBench and SnitchBench supply cited comparisons rather than newly evaluated task streams.

E2.justification: Table 6 adds a Single Turn Auditor comparator for the Context Auditor on Gemini 2.5 Pro, DeepSeek V3.1, GPT-4o-1120, and DeepSeek V3-0324. Model membership in the original main and Activity Planning comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 substantially expands validation design: Appendix B.3 introduces three-expert binary labeling of 10 randomly selected trajectories containing 155 rounds, plus a separate 16-round expert review. Section 5.2 adds immediate-post-event versus trajectory-context auditing, and Figure 5 adds event suppression. The original main-experiment settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New analyses test auditor reliability against humans, sensitivity to available interaction history, and behavior without external events. Appendix A.4 also adds a logged example where trust and comfort diverge. Existing category/pressure controls and appendix case studies are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 3–5 newly report standard errors for supervisor states and pressure/category analyses, and Appendix B.3 introduces Cohen's kappa for human-auditor agreement. The original 20-trial mean-and-standard-error reporting remains. Figure 4's new caption says standard deviation, inconsistently with Table 3's standard-error label.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 are numerically unchanged. Substantial additions include human agreement of 15/16 judgments and kappa 0.732, no-event results, and single-turn auditing scores: GPT-4o-1120 scores 0.511 versus the retained full-context rate of 0.637. Tables 3–5 supply numerical reports for existing analyses, although Table 5 does not consistently match Figure 5.

T1.justification: The structured event-set definition, supervisor-state definition, and feedback equation are unchanged. Added explanations of state distinctions and deception versus hallucination introduce no new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: v3 explicitly claims that models appearing non-deceptive on short-horizon benchmarks can exhibit substantial long-horizon deception, and foregrounds chains of deception invisible to static evaluation. The central framework contribution and claims about model variation, pressure, and trust remain.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive limitations concerning language-only actions and auditing without internal reasoning (A.6), a pressure-based interpretation of falsification versus hallucination (C.1), and discussion of auditor oversensitivity (B.3). It also interprets the new context comparison, although Table 6's blanket higher-severity claim has an exception for Gemini's conditional severity.

D1.justification: v3 explicitly clarifies the absence of tool actions and exclusion of internal chain-of-thought, and documents human-review effort, including three hours for the 16-round review. Existing prompts, data synthesis instructions, hyperparameters, model assignments, and code-access disclosure remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 more specifically distinguishes its interdependent task streams from Scheurer's few-turn deception and Meinke's single-objective scheming. It adds prior theoretical positioning and citations including Carroll and Ward, plus comparisons with DeceptionBench and SnitchBench. The established related-work themes remain.

P1.justification: The framework receives the LH-Deception name; the abstract, introduction, and related work are revised, with some methodological prose shortened. New discussion and appendix subsections alter local organization, while the overall section progression and most existing method/results prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands quantitative presentation through detailed state, pressure, and deception-type tables and the two-part auditor-comparison table. Figure 5 is enlarged and adds 'None' bars; captions gain data references. A critical-pressure example already present in v1's appendix is also displayed in the main text.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked a reported human agreement check for its central auditor. v3's human validation and context comparison provide useful support, while explicit limitations better define applicability. However, three-annotator kappa aggregation is unspecified, Table 5 conflicts with Figure 5, and comparisons across different benchmarks do not isolate horizon effects. These issues limit the quality gain despite the valuable new validation.
